RN-149.title: Orizaba 95 · Brick Hotel
RN-149.current_book:
Luxury boutique hotel with restaurant, listed in the Michelin Guide; at the
corner of Orizaba and Tabasco.
Source notes: Brick Hotel. Built for Sir William Newbold, director of the Banco de Londres y México, reportedly with
bricks brought from England; bought by Álvaro Obregón in 1919 (never lived there; assassinated 1928); brothel in the
1930s-40s; locksmith shop La Moderna (Celso Álvarez) from the 1960s; abandoned; hotel opened 2001, reopened 14
Feb 2020. The name refers to the mustard-colored bricks said to have been shipped from England. The Obregón and
Newbold story comes from press accounts based on the hotel's own history. Wikipedia's History of Colonia Roma
instead says Obregón bought it in 1919 but was killed before living there, that it was a brothel in the 1930s and 1940s,
and that the hotel opened in February 2020.
